name: Modern
summary: Clean lines, large quiet fields of colour, and furniture with light legs.
description: Modern interiors favour open sight-lines, low furniture, and a restrained palette. Floors are usually timber or large-format tile. Lighting is layered: a few architectural fittings plus lamps. Colour sits in one or two stronger pieces rather than on every wall.

name: Traditional
summary: Warm woods, layered textiles, and colours drawn from clay and forest.
description: Traditional rooms accept mouldings, hung art, and furniture with a presence. Floors might be oak or limestone. Paint is seldom pure white — clay, putty, and sage sit more comfortably with brass and woven fabrics. Pattern can appear in a rug or curtains without dominating.

name: Minimalist
summary: Few objects, hidden storage, and a pale envelope that lets light do the work.
description: Minimalist planning is as much about what you omit as what you buy. Surfaces are continuous; handles disappear; furniture is sparse and useful. A single material — plaster, pale timber, or polished concrete — can run across floor and bench. Colour, if used, is a quiet grey-green or a single dark plane.

name: Industrial
summary: Raw structure left visible: metal, concrete, and worn timber.
description: Industrial interiors borrow from workshops: sealed concrete or vinyl that looks like timber, metal shelving, and darker walls that hide services. Comfort comes from textiles and warm lamps so the room does not feel like a store-room. Pair hard floors with a substantial rug in the sitting zone.
